behaviour: Reads ?id= from the URL, fetches that notification and highlights it, showing it alongside the current rows when it is not among them.
rules: No filter, sort, page number or page size state changes because of the id.
An error from the by-id fetch is never rendered and never joins the list's error, so an unknown or inaccessible id leaves the page working normally.
With no id, or an empty id, getNotification is not called and the table gets the list rows unchanged.

behaviour: Covers deep link highlighting on the notifications page.
rules: Render with renderInTestApp(<TestApiProvider apis={[[notificationsApiRef, api], [toastApiRef, { post: jest.fn() }]]}><NotificationsPage /></TestApiProvider>, { routeEntries: ['/notifications?id=...'] }).
The mock API is jest.Mocked<NotificationsApi>; getStatus resolves { unread: 1, read: 0 } and getTopics resolves { topics: [] }.
Find the highlighted row with closest('[aria-current="true"]') from the title element; use the page's default page size of 5 for the capped case.

tests.name: highlights an item that is in the current list
tests.given: The list holds items a and b, getNotification resolves a, and the URL has ?id=a
tests.expect: getNotification is called with 'a'; a's title has an aria-current ancestor, b's does not, and a shows once

tests.name: shows an item outside the current list within the page size
tests.given: The list holds five rows, getNotification resolves a read item not among them, and the URL has its id
tests.expect: The item shows highlighted as the first row, four list rows show and the fifth does not; getNotifications is still called with read false and offset 0

tests.name: keeps working for an unknown id
tests.given: getNotification rejects and the URL has ?id=missing
tests.expect: The list rows show, nothing has aria-current and no error panel shows

tests.name: ignores a missing or empty id
tests.given: One render at /notifications and one at /notifications?id=
tests.expect: The list rows show, getNotification is not called and nothing has aria-current

behaviour: Documents the home page card, how to add it, its refresh behaviour and the deep link.
rules: State that the card is available in the new frontend system only and that it shows the latest 5 unread notifications with a mark-as-read action.

State that installing the plugin provides the widget home-page-widget:notifications/unread-notifications, that it is added to a layout as component UnreadNotifications under defaultConfig of page:home with a short app-config.yaml example, and that setting the extension to false disables it.
State that the card refreshes on notification signals, and polls every 60 seconds only when the signals API is not installed in the app; it does not poll when signals are installed but disconnected.
State that each item links to the notifications page with ?id=<id>, that the page highlights that notification, and that it also shows the notification when it is outside the current filter or page.

sites.rule: Add a blank line, then a '### Home page card' subsection holding the content of this unit's rules.

uses.reason: The defaultConfig shape to copy in the example.

rules: Front matter is exactly one entry: '@backstage/plugin-notifications': patch

The body is: Added an unread notifications card for the home page, available as a home page widget in the new frontend system. The card lists your latest unread notifications, lets you mark them as read, and stays up to date through signals, or by polling when signals are not installed. The notifications page now highlights the notification given by the `id` query parameter.
Front matter is exactly one entry: '@backstage/plugin-home-react': patch
The body is: Home page cards that use a custom `Renderer` no longer need app context to render. While such a card loads, it shows a generic progress indicator instead of the app's progress component.
